name: Clavira — watched folder: photos in, web-ready images out

nodes.name: Every 2 minutes
nodes.notes: Polling, not a filesystem watcher. A watcher fires the instant a file appears — which is while it is still being copied. Polling plus the lock check in intake.ps1 means a batch is only ever claimed once the sender has let go of it.

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.notes:
background: white | transparent | keep.

'white' and 'transparent' only key out a UNIFORM backdrop — a sweep, a lightbox, the black of a CAD render. The processor samples the four corners and, if they disagree, leaves the shot alone and says so. A piece photographed on patterned silk needs a real cutout tool, not a colour key.

pad is the breathing room around the piece, as a fraction of the square.

nodes.name: Claim a batch
nodes.notes: Claiming MOVES files out of drop\ before anything reads them. So a folder dropped in halfway through a run belongs to the next batch rather than being processed half-copied — and files the sender still has open are skipped, not grabbed.

nodes.name: Idle
nodes.notes: Drop folder empty. Most runs end here.

nodes.name: Process images
nodes.notes:
Applies EXIF rotation, keys a uniform backdrop, trims to the piece, centres it on a square, and writes WebP at each size.

--recursive mirrors the sender's folder structure, because a shoot arranged as <SKU>\<frame>.jpg carries the only clue about which piece each file belongs to.

nodes.name: Archive originals
nodes.notes: Originals move to _done\<batch>. They are never deleted — a reprocess at a different size months later needs the full-resolution file, and the processed WebP cannot give it back.

parameters.command: =powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "{{ $('Settings').first().json.scriptDir }}\intake.ps1" -Root "{{ $('Settings').first().json.root }}" -Action fail -Batch "{{ $json.batch }}" -Reason "{{ ($json.stderr || 'No images could be processed.').replaceAll('"','') }}"

nodes.name: Quarantine batch
nodes.notes: Originals go to _failed\<batch> WITH a why.txt. A folder of files and no explanation is worse than useless six weeks later.
